## Definition

- **Tier:** `anchored`
- **Semantic types:** `T019`, `T020`, `T033`, `T037`, `T046`, `T047`, `T048`, `T049`, `T050`, `T184`, `T191`
- **Children:** [`disease`](disease_NER_validation.md), [`symptom`](symptom_NER_validation.md), [`finding`](finding_NER_validation.md)
- **Counts toward `clinical_any`:** yes
- **Development-corpus prevalence:** 21.1% of content tokens, 1,940 distinct word types ([measured](../../measurements/category_prevalence.json))

## Definition in words

Anything wrong with the patient: diagnoses, syndromes, injuries, and the signs and symptoms that evidence them. The parent every gold standard actually adjudicates, which is why validation happens here and its three children are treated as refinements of a validated boundary.

A gold standard adjudicates this category directly. Precision, recall and F1 can be reported against expert annotations.

## Benchmark

### [i2b2/VA 2010 concept extraction](https://portal.dbmi.hms.harvard.edu/projects/n2c2-nlp/)

- **Maps to:** `problem`
- **Corpus:** Partners, Beth Israel Deaconess and UPMC notes
- **Size:** 170 training / 256 test summaries
- **Access:** DBMI data-use agreement
- **Paper:** https://doi.org/10.1136/amiajnl-2011-000203

Three categories only: problem, test, treatment. `treatment` covers both procedures and drugs, so it can only ever partially anchor either.

### [ShARe/CLEF eHealth 2013-2014](https://physionet.org/content/shareclefehealth2013/)

- **Maps to:** `disorder`
- **Corpus:** clinical notes
- **Size:** 298 notes (2013 task 1)
- **Access:** PhysioNet credentialed
- **Paper:** https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-40802-1_24

Disorders plus ten contextual attributes. Also the corpus QuickUMLS itself was evaluated on, so it doubles as the check that our configuration reproduces published behaviour.

### [SNOMED CT Entity Linking Challenge](https://physionet.org/content/snomed-ct-entity-challenge/)

- **Maps to:** `clinical finding`
- **Corpus:** 272 MIMIC-IV discharge notes
- **Size:** 75,491 annotations of 6,595 concepts as released (74,808 / 6,624 as published)
- **Access:** PhysioNet credentialed
- **Paper:** https://doi.org/10.1093/jamia/ocaf104

Six clinical annotators, ~70% double-annotated with a third adjudicating disagreements. Same corpus family as the development notes, which is why it is the primary anchor.

### Protocol

Per [`validation/protocol.md`](../../protocol.md):

1. Tag the gold corpus, map gold labels onto this category via the crosswalk above.
2. Report **targeting precision** first — of the edits placed under this category, what fraction hit a gold span of the mapped label. This is the package's actual claim.
3. Report strict and relaxed P/R/F1 for completeness, with cluster-bootstrap CIs **by `patient_id`**.
4. Run the L0-L4 ablation so each method addition gets a number.

L3 and L4 are measured, but **not per category**: their gold is
span-level assertion rather than category membership, so a
category-stratified split would need assertion gold no available corpus
supplies. Corpus-level values are in `assertion_accuracy.json` (L3,
negated-class F1 0.9289 against a 0.0000 floor) and
`assertion_deid_invariance.json` (L4, instability 0.0000 against
PyRuSH's 0.1429).
